boundary: Evidence interpretation only. Original method reports, judge decisions and ledger entries remain frozen; no finding feeds back into method execution.

facts: Both reports describe the same authored root initial edge to PoweredOff and a separate PoweredOff-to-Operate transition triggered by start.
Both reports require the root initial edge to target Operate directly. Their titles, citations and wording differ.
Round 1 is INVALID/D0: the judge accepts the structural fact but reads start as the turn-on signal, allowing PoweredOff before power-on.
Round 2 is VALID_NOVEL/D2: the judge reads powering on as an obligation on the root initial edge, rejecting the later start transition as a substitute.
Both method cells were generated on the old provider. The two judge cells use different registered provider profiles and were called at different times.
cases.interpretation: The disputed step is the normative inference from power-on to unconditional root initialization, not the existence of the authored edges. The recorded classifications demonstrate sensitivity to requirement interpretation and report/judge conditions.
cases.causal_limit: Report wording, judge provider and judge time vary together. This comparison does not identify a provider effect or prove that disabling predicates caused a factual hallucination.

facts: The cell emits 10 reports, classified as 1 K, 9 N and 0 I.
Issues 2 and 7 both claim that Interception_Detected has declared consumer transition:line:24 but no reachable consumer. One uses a scope locus, the other an event locus.
Issues 3 and 8 both claim that Task_Assignment_Received has declared consumer transition:line:25 but no reachable consumer, again with scope versus event loci.
The paired reports have different derived contract IDs and neither pair was folded into one published report.

Issue 10 separately reports the unreachable operating scope and includes a folded event-consumer consequence. Its root scope is named UAVSwarmStateMachine, whereas other reports use the natural-language name UAV swarm operation.
cases.interpretation: N counts valid reports outside the ledger, including overlapping claims. Differences in contract identity and locus representation survive the existing publication merge, so these nine N reports cannot be read as nine independent new defects.
cases.causal_limit: The audit establishes concrete report overlap. It does not assign a unique defect count, change K/N/I, or isolate how much of the overlap was caused by the predicate ablation.

facts: Round-1 contract_completion admitted no additional contract or transition group.
Round-1 discovery_grounding branch 0 introduced additional PumpState and WaterState default-entry obligations. Its basis inferred unconditional entry from the required pump and monitoring behavior.
The method published these two claims at internal D2. The external judge retained the authored trigger facts but rejected the unconditional-entry obligation, classifying both as INVALID/D0.
Round 2 published closely corresponding PumpState and WaterState unconditional-entry claims and another for MethaneState.

The round-2 judge likewise classified their core defect class as D0 but assigned FULL relations to INS-0002-03, INS-0002-04 and INS-0002-05. Under the same relation-first closure, all three final report classes are VALID_KNOWN.
The two rounds use the same frozen judge protocol hash and closure settings. The sampled report wording, judge provider, invocation time and relation decisions differ.
cases.interpretation: There are two distinct issues: grounding can infer a stronger normative obligation than the cited NL states, and relation-first ownership can classify a D0 report as K after a positive ledger relation. The strict D2/D1 sensitivity excludes these reports while the main K/N/I accounting retains the frozen labels.
cases.causal_limit: These are traced generation and adjudication facts, not an isolated causal estimate of predicate value or provider quality. No judge result, expected relation or ledger item is rewritten to remove the discrepancy.
